label: D24-rantai-audit
decision: For Anastrophe's tamper-evident audit log (FR-54, SDD §8.1 table audit_events with prev_hash/hash), should the hash chain be one global chain for the whole deployment or one chain per site?

candidates.description: One chain across all sites: each new row's prev_hash is the hash of the latest row in the table. Appends are serialized deployment-wide (one advisory lock). Verifying any site's audit export requires the whole chain.

One chain per site: audit_events gets a site_id column and prev_hash links to the latest row of the same site. Appends serialize only within a site (advisory lock per site). Each site's audit view/export (GET /admin/sites/{id}/audit) is verifiable on its own. Events not tied to a site (e.g. account.deleted) go to a separate platform chain.

priorities: 1) Tamper evidence that a site's auditor can verify for their own site without seeing other tenants' data. 2) Fit the SDD data model and the per-site audit API. 3) Simplicity of implementation and verification. 4) Avoid a deployment-wide write bottleneck. The user approved autonomous iteration; decisions under 0.60 go back to the user.
requirements: A site's audit export can be verified end to end without access to other sites' audit rows.
Appending an audit event never needs a lock shared by all sites.
Every audit row still links to the previous row of its chain, so deleting or editing any row is detectable.
